run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-18T02:15:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: Observed facts: frontend-proxy's ingress spans on the checkout path failed with http.status_code 504 / otel.status_code ERROR after ~15.0 s, and its own Envoy log lines read '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000'. The chain shown in trace 87fccd70d595ebdd9b6b292d102b1f67 runs frontend-proxy ingress (504, 15.000156 s) above frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (30.083680 s) and checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (30.062113 s), whose child 'HTTP POST' client span lasted 30.000210 s with otel.status_code ERROR and description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; cart, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and quote calls in the same trace returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in milliseconds. 100.67.49.77:8080 is the email Service ClusterIP. checkout logs repeat 'failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'. frontend-proxy ingress error increase over 10 m was 3.2-4.5 before 02:15, then 102.1 at 02:20:12, 218.9 at 02:25:12 and 110.3 at 02:30:12. Chaos-mesh events are the only evidence naming the fault: a Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh spawned NetworkChaos objects every minute 02:15:02Z-02:22:02Z, and each 'Applied' message names otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn and otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, with 'TimeUp'/'Recovered' about 55 s later. Hypothesis (best supported): that Schedule causes the timeouts; the frontend-proxy 504s are a downstream consequence, not a frontend-proxy fault. Conclusion is partial because the fault object is known only from events, the chaos CRD specs and any chaos after 02:22:18 were not observable, and the alert rule itself is not loaded in this Prometheus.

claims.text: frontend-proxy recorded error ingress spans on the checkout path: http.status_code 504, otel.status_code ERROR, error=true, each lasting ~15,001,4xx microseconds (e.g. span 317f5eeff095f1f6 duration_us 15001496).

The frontend-proxy container log lines show '"POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 504 UT response_timeout ... 15000' against upstream frontend:8080 (260 matching '504' lines in the 02:14-02:22 window; e.g. 02:22:09.321603Z and 02:22:32.213198Z).

In trace 87fccd70d595ebdd9b6b292d102b1f67 the proxy ingress span (504, 15.000156 s) and egress span (http.status_code 0, 14.999989 s) sit above frontend 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (30.083680 s) and checkout 'oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder' (30.062113 s), whose child 'HTTP POST' client span lasted 30.000210 s with otel.status_code ERROR and description 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout'; cart, product-catalog, currency, payment, shipping and quote calls in the same trace returned rpc.grpc.status_code 0 in milliseconds.

checkout error spans carry the same diagnostic: 'HTTP POST' spans with otel.status_code ERROR and error detail 'dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' at ~30,000,2xx microseconds, e.g. spans 09813367d275caee, 48bbd666994fc75d, 75cd8be0f0ddde53.

The checkout container log states the failing dependency explicitly: 'failed to send order confirmation ...: failed POST to email service: Post "http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation": dial tcp 100.67.49.77:8080: i/o timeout' (268 matching lines in 02:14-02:22; shown slice 02:22:36.515684061Z-02:22:51.730908027Z).
The dial target 100.67.49.77:8080 is the 'email' Service in otel-demo (clusterIP 100.67.49.77, port 8080).

A chaos-mesh Schedule named otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition in namespace chaos-mesh spawned NetworkChaos objects once per minute: 'Create new object: otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj' at 02:15:02Z, then -hddgv 02:16:02Z, -mznpj 02:17:02Z, -zl9p2 02:18:02Z, -7rvkf 02:19:02Z, -8p7rs 02:20:02Z, -4f5lv 02:21:02Z, -5c2dr 02:22:02Z.

Each NetworkChaos object applied the fault to the two email pods and the checkout pod, e.g. for otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition-jdmmj at 02:15:02Z: 'Successfully apply chaos for otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn', '... otel-demo/email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w', '... otel-demo/checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs', followed by 'Time up according to the duration' and 'Successfully recover chaos' for the same three pods at 02:15:57Z.

PodNetworkChaos events in namespace otel-demo record 'Successfully update ObservedGeneration and FailedMessage of resource' for exactly the same three pods (checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs, email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w, email-59f69bc6cf-db9mn) at each minute boundary 02:15:02Z-02:22:02Z, with no other pods listed.

frontend-proxy ingress error counts rose out of a low baseline: increase over 10 m was 4.5 at 02:00:12, 4.2 at 02:05:12, 3.2 at 02:10:12, 4.2 at 02:15:12, then 102.1 at 02:20:12, 218.9 at 02:25:12 and 110.3 at 02:30:12.

At 02:26:00 the only non-zero error-span increases in the 15 m window were frontend-proxy 'ingress' (220.79) and checkout 'HTTP POST' (100.94); frontend spans 'GET', 'POST', 'POST /api/checkout', 'executing api route (pages) /api/checkout', 'grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder', payment 'dns.lookup' and accounting 'orders receive' were 0, while flagd EventStream series showed a steady ~1-2 per 10 m also present before the incident.
The email service's span counters in 01:57-02:33 contain only status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET; no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series was returned for service_name="email".

At query time all otel-demo workloads were running and ready with 0 restarts, including frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-jft59, frontend-675fd7b5c5-kzdpp, checkout-5dccddf8bb-9cgqs and the two email pods; the email pods were created 2026-11-18T01:41:54Z, before the incident, and are owned by ReplicaSet email-59f69bc6cf.

All flagd flags in ConfigMap flagd-config (key demo.flagd.json) had defaultVariant "off" when read (all variants including imageSlowLoad, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, emailMemoryLeak, productCatalogFailure, cartFailure, adFailure).

The alert coincided with the first applied chaos: the first NetworkChaos of Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition started at 02:15:02Z and the alert anchor is 02:15:12Z, while frontend-proxy 504s require the ~15 s proxy timeout to elapse first.

email was not crashing or restarting in a way visible here: both email pods are ready with restartCount 0 and the email Service has two ready endpoint addresses (100.96.2.7, 100.96.3.218); the failure is a dial i/o timeout, not connection refused, so this is a packet-path problem rather than a down process.

Best-supported cause: the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition repeatedly applies a network partition between the email pods and the checkout pod; checkout's POST to http://email:8080/send_order_confirmation then blocks on a 30 s dial timeout, checkout's PlaceOrder hangs ~30 s, the frontend's /api/checkout exceeds frontend-proxy's 15 s route timeout, and frontend-proxy emits 504s, which is what RequestErrorRate measured.

Rejected: an enabled flagd fault-injection flag caused the failures. All flags in demo.flagd.json were defaultVariant "off", and the services those flags target (payment, ad, cart, product-catalog, recommendation) show no ERROR spans in the incident window; the failure is a dial timeout to the email Service.

Rejected: frontend-proxy itself was the failing component (bad config or crash). Its deployment still runs image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-frontend-proxy with 1/1 ready and pod restarts 0, its egress spans carry http.status_code 0 meaning no upstream response, and the slow span sits below it in checkout waiting on email.

Inspect the chaos-mesh Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and the NetworkChaos objects it spawns (specs, direction, duration, and whether the schedule is still active) through the chaos-mesh API, since the current tool set cannot read those CRDs.

Align timeouts so an unreachable email service fails fast: checkout's observed 30 s dial timeout exceeds frontend-proxy's observed 15000 ms route timeout, so every email outage becomes a client-visible 504 and raises RequestErrorRate on frontend-proxy.

gaps: Chaos-mesh CRDs (Schedule and NetworkChaos specs: partition direction, loss/delay values, duration, selectors beyond the pod names in messages) are not readable with the available resource kinds; fault scope is inferred from event messages and pod names only.
Event data ends at 02:22:18Z, while frontend-proxy 504s continued to about 02:25; the NetworkChaos instances after 02:22:02Z and the moment chaos stopped are unknown.

list_prometheus_rules with rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned nothing (no_data), so the alert expression and the annotation's value 0.2444 are unverified; the alert payload was treated as an untrusted lead only.
fetch_pod_logs for frontend-675fd7b5c5-kzdpp and email-59f69bc6cf-6sl4w returned no lines for 02:10-02:33 (status no_data), so application-log evidence for those two services is missing.

The NetworkPolicy query for otel-demo returned nothing (status no_data), so the absence of policies blocking port 8080 is unchecked rather than proven; connectivity loss rests on the chaos events and the i/o timeouts.

Email request activity during each partition minute is unknown: the 1-minute increase query for service_name="email" returned 0 at every sampled point (02:01:12-02:25:12) while the 10-minute query returned non-zero values, so these series do not quantify email traffic.

Some trace/log reads were truncated (read_evidence marked incomplete/truncated for the frontend-proxy span list, checkout error-span list and frontend-proxy 504 log lines), so only the shown slices were examined.
next_steps: Query the chaos-mesh API for Schedule otel-demo-email-checkout-network-partition and its NetworkChaos children to confirm fault parameters and whether it is still scheduled.

Confirm frontend-proxy route timeout (15000 ms) and checkout-to-email HTTP/dial timeouts, and consider reducing the email call timeout below the proxy timeout so failures surface as fast gRPC errors instead of 504s.
Review load-generator checkout results for the 02:15-02:25 window to size client-visible impact of the 504s.
